blocks.heading: Where could Gilead Sciences' shares be by October 2029?

paragraphs.text: The weighted forecast is $124.65 by October 2027, a 15% loss. It reaches $141.61 by October 2029, a 1% gain. Bear probability is 25%; base probability is 55%. Bull probability is 20%. The October 2029 range runs from $57.85 to $247.96.

blocks.heading: What drives Gilead Sciences' base, bear and bull cases?

paragraphs.text: The base holds margins near the 2025 adjusted level of about 34.8%, because HIV remains strong and acquired-research charges fade. Management guided to 9%–10% HIV growth and $1bn of Yeztugo sales for 2026. The bear assumes rising discounts, weak Yeztugo persistence, declining Veklury and limited oncology gains. The bull assumes prevention, oncology and cell therapy improve together. Adjusted earnings beat consensus in all eight reviewed quarters, supporting the base case but not guaranteeing the bull case.

The bear case requires weakness in Gilead’s largest franchise and several pipeline disappointments at once. HIV growth slows as discounts rise, Yeztugo repeat use falls short, oncology contributes little and cell therapy continues to decline. Debt then limits buybacks, while investors apply a lower multiple.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Gilead Sciences really make?

paragraphs.text: In 2025, operating cash flow was $10,019 million. Capital spending was $563 million, leaving free cash flow of $9,456 million, or 32.1% of revenue. Free cash flow nevertheless declined from $10,305 million in 2024 while reported net income rose sharply. The difference comes from timing and non-cash accounting.

Stock-based compensation was $894 million. Gilead adds it back because issuing shares does not immediately use cash, but employees still receive part of the business. Subtracting it gives an analytical “real free cash flow” figure of $8,562 million, or 29.1% of revenue.

blocks.heading: How much does Gilead Sciences pay per share?

paragraphs.text: Dividends rise from $3.37 per share to $3.48 and $3.60 in the base case. The bear holds each period at $3.28, reflecting the current $0.82 quarterly rate and higher debt. The bull reaches $3.40, $3.56 and $3.72 as HIV cash generation strengthens. The base follows the recent 3.8% increase and a five-year record of annual growth.

blocks.heading: Does Gilead Sciences cover its dividend with cash?

paragraphs.text: Shareholders received $25,058 million through dividends and buybacks. Dividends reached $4,003 million in 2025. Buybacks reached $1,922 million that year. Together, those payments absorbed 62.7% of that year’s free cash flow and left $3,531 million for other uses. Dividends deliver cash immediately. Buybacks can increase each remaining share’s claim on future earnings, but only if Gilead buys at sensible prices.

Stock-based compensation was $894 million. Gilead adds it back because issuing shares does not immediately use cash, but employees still receive part of the business. Subtracting it gives an analytical “real free cash flow” figure of $8,562 million, or 29.1% of revenue.

blocks.heading: What could change Gilead Sciences' dividend?

paragraphs.text: The first evidence would come from HIV demand, net pricing and Yeztugo repeat dosing during 2027–2029. Slower treatment growth, larger payer discounts or weaker persistence would move the forecast toward the bear case. Stronger prevention uptake and external patient starts would support the bull case.

Finally, cash conversion, debt repayment and repurchase activity will show whether acquisitions create value. Sustained cash generation with lower debt would support faster buybacks and valuation expansion. Elevated debt and restrained repurchases would reinforce the bear path.

blocks.heading: What has Gilead Sciences guided for the year?

paragraphs.text: Gilead’s weighted path is a 15% loss by October 2027 and a 1% gain by October 2029, hinging on durable HIV cash flow and returns from new products and acquisitions. Management guides to 2026 product sales of $30,100–$30,400 million. It expects HIV sales growth of 9%–10% and Yeztugo sales of $1,000 million. Guidance also carries diluted loss per share of $3.75–$3.40 against illustrative non-GAAP diluted EPS of $8.50–$8.85.

blocks.heading: What trend do Gilead Sciences' recent results show?

paragraphs.text: Revenue reached $7,803 million, compared with $7,082 million a year earlier. Reported growth was 10.2%, but $156 million came from recognizing previously constrained intellectual-property sale revenue. Excluding that item, revenue was $7,647 million and growth was 8.0%. The accounting release concerned an earlier transaction, not new Biktarvy, Trodelvy or Yeztugo demand.

The reported net loss was $10,496 million. Acquired research included approximately $7,000 million for one program and $3,100 million for another. A third acquired program added approximately $1,900 million. An $860 million Lakefront reimbursement reduced acquired-research expense rather than appearing as revenue. Trodelvy also suffered a further $1,750 million impairment. These items explain why adjusted EPS remained negative at $6.75, even though management illustrated approximately $2.27 after excluding the acquisitions and other non-recurring items.

blocks.heading: What should Gilead Sciences watchers look for next?

paragraphs.text: The next quarterly report should test Yeztugo’s progress toward its annual target and show whether cell-therapy sales are stabilizing. Operating cash generation and debt reduction matter just as much as reported earnings.
